【Course profile】
・Each class has a maximum of 4 students.
・Lessons are offered twice a week (Saturday intensives are offered once a week, 2 periods in a row).
・Schedules differ between campuses, and each section is held only on one campus. Once course registration is complete, it cannot be changed.
・The course uses Tutorial Canvas, which can be accessed through the “Classes” tab under “Learning Support” on MyWaseda. Please note that Tutorial Canvas may not function properly on PCs that do not meet the system requirements.
The course is designed for students who fit one or more of the following descriptions:
・TOEFL iBT（Speaking）score: 4 to 4.5 *taken on/before Jan 20, 2026: 20 to 24
・TOEIC S&W（Speaking）score: 160 to 179
・Who are aiming to communicate fluently and spontaneously
・Who are aiming to express ideas logically and precisely when discussing complex subjects
・Who are aiming to sustain English proficiency after coming back from studying abroad
・Who are aiming to improve English skill for working in an international field in the future
【Levels】
Students are placed in levels and grouped into classes based on the results of the LANGX Test, which is taken during a specified period. The 4 levels are Basic, Intermediate, Upper Intermediate, and Advanced. The first three (Basic, Intermediate, and Upper Intermediate) are completed in four quarters A, B, C and D, which should be taken consecutively.
・Advanced is completed in two quarters, A and B, which should be taken consecutively.
It is recommended that students begin the course in spring semester, taking A and B consecutively. Then during the fall semester registration period, students should register for C and D.
For students taking the course as an elective:
Students select the level of the course, which cannot be changed after registration. The LANGX test must be taken from the class registration screen at this time. Students can only register for A or C during the 1st registration period and need to take the test during the 1st registration period. Click “入力有” under “備考欄” to take the LANGX test.
For students who are required to take the course:
Student levels are determined by their LANGX Test scores. Compulsory students must take the LANGX Test during the designated testing period.
Please see https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html (LANGX test periods)

①
Preparation
Before each class, students must complete the Preparation activities on Tutorial Canvas (about 40–60 minutes). These activities help students think about the topic in advance and prepare to participate actively in class.
②
In class
All classes are held on campus. Students practice conversations through pair and group work, as well as role-play activities. Students are assessed on their interactions in class, which include turn-taking, active listening, and working with others. Assessment scores and feedback will be posted on Tutorial Canvas.
③
Test Unit
Units 5 and 10 are designated as Test Units:
Unit 5: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 1–4.
Unit 10: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 6–9.
The lesson flow in Test Units is similar to regular units, but students will be specifically evaluated on whether they can use the target Can-dos correctly and effectively.
④
Final Review Sheet
After the quarter, students will receive a Final Review Sheet from each tutor. It will include comments on the student’s progress and strengths, along with advice for future study.
⑤
LANGX (Post-Course)　(approx. 30 minutes)
After Unit 10, students are required to take the LANGX test again to assess their progress.
The following are the topics for each unit.
Unit 1 Descriptions and Narratives
Unit 2 Significant Events and Experiences
Unit 3 Cultural Viewpoints and Practices
Unit 4 Evaluating Problems, Challenges, and Proposals
Unit 5 Test Unit (Unit 1-4)
Unit 6 Summarizing Opinion Pieces
Unit 7 Formal Discussions
Unit 8 Requests and Permission
Unit 9 Describing and Interpreting Data
Unit 10 Test Unit (Unit 6-9)

https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html

・Each class has a maximum of 4 students.
・Lessons are offered twice a week (Saturday intensives are offered once a week, 2 periods in a row).
・Schedules differ between campuses, and each section is held only on one campus. Once course registration is complete, it cannot be changed.
・The course uses Tutorial Canvas, which can be accessed through the “Classes” tab under “Learning Support” on MyWaseda. Please note that Tutorial Canvas may not function properly on PCs that do not meet the system requirements.

・TOEFL iBT（Speaking）score: 4 to 4.5 *taken on/before Jan 20, 2026: 20 to 24
・TOEIC S&W（Speaking）score: 160 to 179
・Who are aiming to communicate fluently and spontaneously
・Who are aiming to express ideas logically and precisely when discussing complex subjects
・Who are aiming to sustain English proficiency after coming back from studying abroad
・Who are aiming to improve English skill for working in an international field in the future
【Levels】
Students are placed in levels and grouped into classes based on the results of the LANGX Test, which is taken during a specified period. The 4 levels are Basic, Intermediate, Upper Intermediate, and Advanced. ・Advanced is completed in two quarters, A and B, which should be taken consecutively.
It is recommended that students begin the course in spring semester, taking A and B consecutively. Then during the fall semester registration period, students should register for C and D.
For students taking the course as an elective:
Students select the level of the course, which cannot be changed after registration. The LANGX test must be taken from the class registration screen at this time. Students can only register for A or C during the 1st registration period and need to take the test during the 1st registration period. Click “入力有” under “備考欄” to take the LANGX test.
For students who are required to take the course:
Student levels are determined by their LANGX Test scores. Compulsory students must take the LANGX Test during the designated testing period.
Please see https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html (LANGX test periods)

Each class has specific “Can-dos” (learning goals). To achieve the Can-dos, students will learn vocabulary and expressions and practice using them in conversations.
①
Preparation
Before each class, students must complete the Preparation activities on Tutorial Canvas (about 40–60 minutes). These activities help students think about the topic in advance and prepare to participate actively in class.
②
In class
All classes are held on campus. Students practice conversations through pair and group work, as well as role-play activities. Students are assessed on their interactions in class, which include turn-taking, active listening, and working with others. Assessment scores and feedback will be posted on Tutorial Canvas.
③
Test Unit
Units 5 and 10 are designated as Test Units:
Unit 5: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 1–4.
Unit 10: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 6–9.
The lesson flow in Test Units is similar to regular units, but students will be specifically evaluated on whether they can use the target Can-dos correctly and effectively.
④
Final Review Sheet
After the quarter, students will receive a Final Review Sheet from each tutor. It will include comments on the student’s progress and strengths, along with advice for future study.
⑤
LANGX (Post-Course)　(approx. 30 minutes)
After Unit 10, students are required to take the LANGX test again to assess their progress.
The following are the topics for each unit.
Unit 1 Descriptions and Narratives
Unit 2 Significant Events and Experiences
Unit 3 Cultural Viewpoints and Practices
Unit 4 Evaluating Problems, Challenges, and Proposals
Unit 5 Test Unit (Unit 1-4)
Unit 6 Summarizing Opinion Pieces
Unit 7 Formal Discussions
Unit 8 Requests and Permission
Unit 9 Describing and Interpreting Data
Unit 10 Test Unit (Unit 6-9)

1.  Pre-Course LANGX test (approximately 30 minutes)
Please take the LANGX Test during the designated period. If you do not take the test, you may not be able to enroll in the appropriate level or class.
2.  Class announcements
Information about tutors, class days, times, and locations will be posted on Tutorial Canvas. Announcements will be made in the evening on the following dates:
Fall quarter: October 1 late afternoon
3.  Class meetings
Each class has specific “Can-dos” (learning goals). To achieve the Can-dos, students will learn vocabulary and expressions and practice using them in conversations.
①
Preparation
Before each class, students must complete the Preparation activities on Tutorial Canvas (about 40–60 minutes). These activities help students think about the topic in advance and prepare to participate actively in class.
②
In class
All classes are held on campus. Students practice conversations through pair and group work, as well as role-play activities. Students are assessed on their interactions in class, which include turn-taking, active listening, and working with others. Assessment scores and feedback will be posted on Tutorial Canvas.
③
Test Unit
Units 5 and 10 are designated as Test Units:
Unit 5: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 1–4.
Unit 10: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 6–9.
The lesson flow in Test Units is similar to regular units, but students will be specifically evaluated on whether they can use the target Can-dos correctly and effectively.
④
Final Review Sheet
After the quarter, students will receive a Final Review Sheet from each tutor. It will include comments on the student’s progress and strengths, along with advice for future study.
⑤
LANGX (Post-Course)　(approx. 30 minutes)
After Unit 10, students are required to take the LANGX test again to assess their progress.
The following are the topics for each unit.
Unit 1 Descriptions and Narratives
Unit 2 Significant Events and Experiences
Unit 3 Cultural Viewpoints and Practices
Unit 4 Evaluating Problems, Challenges, and Proposals
Unit 5 Test Unit (Unit 1-4)
Unit 6 Summarizing Opinion Pieces
Unit 7 Formal Discussions
Unit 8 Requests and Permission
Unit 9 Describing and Interpreting Data
Unit 10 Test Unit (Unit 6-9)

summary:
This course aims to develop students’ English communicative ability. Classes are small, with a maximum of 4 students, and meet on campus twice a week for 5 weeks. For details, please refer to the Guide to Tutorial English A–D ＜Quarter Course＞(hereinafter “the Student Guide”).
https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html
【Course profile】
・Each class has a maximum of 4 students.
・Lessons are offered twice a week (Saturday intensives are offered once a week, 2 periods in a row).
・Schedules differ between campuses, and each section is held only on one campus. Once course registration is complete, it cannot be changed.
・The course uses Tutorial Canvas, which can be accessed through the “Classes” tab under “Learning Support” on MyWaseda. Please note that Tutorial Canvas may not function properly on PCs that do not meet the system requirements.
The course is designed for students who fit one or more of the following descriptions:
・TOEFL iBT（Speaking）score: 4 to 4.5 *taken on/before Jan 20, 2026: 20 to 24
・TOEIC S&W（Speaking）score: 160 to 179
・Who are aiming to communicate fluently and spontaneously
・Who are aiming to express ideas logically and precisely when discussing complex subjects
・Who are aiming to sustain English proficiency after coming back from studying abroad
・Who are aiming to improve English skill for working in an international field in the future
【Levels】
Students are placed in levels and grouped into classes based on the results of the LANGX Test, which is taken during a specified period. The 4 levels are Basic, Intermediate, Upper Intermediate, and Advanced. The first three (Basic, Intermediate, and Upper Intermediate) are completed in four quarters A, B, C and D, which should be taken consecutively.
・Advanced is completed in two quarters, A and B, which should be taken consecutively.
It is recommended that students begin the course in spring semester, taking A and B consecutively. Then during the fall semester registration period, students should register for C and D.
For students taking the course as an elective:
Students select the level of the course, which cannot be changed after registration. The LANGX test must be taken from the class registration screen at this time. Students can only register for A or C during the 1st registration period and need to take the test during the 1st registration period. Click “入力有” under “備考欄” to take the LANGX test.
For students who are required to take the course:
Student levels are determined by their LANGX Test scores. Compulsory students must take the LANGX Test during the designated testing period.
Please see https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html (LANGX test periods)
【Schedule】
Lessons offered twice a week
A lesson is offered on Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday for the first half of the week. The other lesson will be offered on Thursday, Friday or Saturday.

・Who are aiming to sustain English proficiency after coming back from studying abroad

Students select the level of the course, which cannot be changed after registration. The LANGX test must be taken from the class registration screen at this time. Students can only register for A or C during the 1st registration period and need to take the test during the 1st registration period. Click “入力有” under “備考欄” to take the LANGX test.

①
Preparation
Before each class, students must complete the Preparation activities on Tutorial Canvas (about 40–60 minutes). These activities help students think about the topic in advance and prepare to participate actively in class.
②
In class
All classes are held on campus. Students practice conversations through pair and group work, as well as role-play activities. Students are assessed on their interactions in class, which include turn-taking, active listening, and working with others. Assessment scores and feedback will be posted on Tutorial Canvas.
③
Test Unit

Unit 5: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 1–4.
Unit 10: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 6–9.

④

After the quarter, students will receive a Final Review Sheet from each tutor. It will include comments on the student’s progress and strengths, along with advice for future study.
⑤
LANGX (Post-Course)　(approx. 30 minutes)
After Unit 10, students are required to take the LANGX test again to assess their progress.

Unit 1 Descriptions and Narratives
Unit 2 Significant Events and Experiences
Unit 3 Cultural Viewpoints and Practices
Unit 4 Evaluating Problems, Challenges, and Proposals
Unit 5 Test Unit (Unit 1-4)
Unit 6 Summarizing Opinion Pieces
Unit 7 Formal Discussions
Unit 8 Requests and Permission
Unit 9 Describing and Interpreting Data
Unit 10 Test Unit (Unit 6-9)

https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html
【Course profile】
・Each class has a maximum of 4 students.
・Lessons are offered twice a week (Saturday intensives are offered once a week, 2 periods in a row).
・Schedules differ between campuses, and each section is held only on one campus. Once course registration is complete, it cannot be changed.
・The course uses Tutorial Canvas, which can be accessed through the “Classes” tab under “Learning Support” on MyWaseda. Please note that Tutorial Canvas may not function properly on PCs that do not meet the system requirements.
The course is designed for students who fit one or more of the following descriptions:
・TOEFL iBT（Speaking）score: 4 to 4.5 *taken on/before Jan 20, 2026: 20 to 24
・TOEIC S&W（Speaking）score: 160 to 179
・Who are aiming to communicate fluently and spontaneously
・Who are aiming to express ideas logically and precisely when discussing complex subjects
・Who are aiming to sustain English proficiency after coming back from studying abroad
・Who are aiming to improve English skill for working in an international field in the future
【Levels】
Students are placed in levels and grouped into classes based on the results of the LANGX Test, which is taken during a specified period. The 4 levels are Basic, Intermediate, Upper Intermediate, and Advanced. The first three (Basic, Intermediate, and Upper Intermediate) are completed in four quarters A, B, C and D, which should be taken consecutively.
・Advanced is completed in two quarters, A and B, which should be taken consecutively.
It is recommended that students begin the course in spring semester, taking A and B consecutively. Then during the fall semester registration period, students should register for C and D.
For students taking the course as an elective:
Students select the level of the course, which cannot be changed after registration. The LANGX test must be taken from the class registration screen at this time. Students can only register for A or C during the 1st registration period and need to take the test during the 1st registration period. Click “入力有” under “備考欄” to take the LANGX test.
For students who are required to take the course:
Student levels are determined by their LANGX Test scores. Compulsory students must take the LANGX Test during the designated testing period.
Please see https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html (LANGX test periods)

Lessons offered twice a week
A lesson is offered on Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday for the first half of the week. The other lesson will be offered on Thursday, Friday or Saturday.

schedule_plan:
The course flow below is the same for both elective and compulsory students:
1.  Pre-Course LANGX test (approximately 30 minutes)
Please take the LANGX Test during the designated period. If you do not take the test, you may not be able to enroll in the appropriate level or class.
2.  Class announcements
Information about tutors, class days, times, and locations will be posted on Tutorial Canvas. Announcements will be made in the evening on the following dates:
Winter quarter : November 16 late afternoon
3.  Class meetings
Each class has specific “Can-dos” (learning goals). To achieve the Can-dos, students will learn vocabulary and expressions and practice using them in conversations.
①
Preparation
Before each class, students must complete the Preparation activities on Tutorial Canvas (about 40–60 minutes). These activities help students think about the topic in advance and prepare to participate actively in class.
②
In class
All classes are held on campus. Students practice conversations through pair and group work, as well as role-play activities. Students are assessed on their interactions in class, which include turn-taking, active listening, and working with others. Assessment scores and feedback will be posted on Tutorial Canvas.
③
Test Unit
Units 5 and 10 are designated as Test Units:
Unit 5: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 1–4.
Unit 10: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 6–9.
The lesson flow in Test Units is similar to regular units, but students will be specifically evaluated on whether they can use the target Can-dos correctly and effectively.
④
Final Review Sheet
After the quarter, students will receive a Final Review Sheet from each tutor. It will include comments on the student’s progress and strengths, along with advice for future study.
⑤
LANGX (Post-Course)　(approx. 30 minutes)
After Unit 10, students are required to take the LANGX test again to assess their progress.
The following are the topics for each unit.
Unit 1 Dramatic Plots
Unit 2 Expressing Reactions to Creative Works
Unit 3 Compensation
Unit 4 Expanding and Supporting Ideas
Unit 5 Test Unit (Unit 1-4)
Unit 6 Social Issues
Unit 7 Compromising
Unit 8 Developing Arguments
Unit 9 Being Diplomatic
Unit 10 Test Unit (Unit 6-9)

summary:
This course aims to develop students’ English communicative ability. Classes are small, with a maximum of 4 students, and meet on campus twice a week for 5 weeks. For details, please refer to the Guide to Tutorial English A–D ＜Quarter Course＞(hereinafter “the Student Guide”).
https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html
【Course profile】
・Each class has a maximum of 4 students.
・Lessons are offered twice a week (Saturday intensives are offered once a week, 2 periods in a row).
・Schedules differ between campuses, and each section is held only on one campus. Once course registration is complete, it cannot be changed.
・The course uses Tutorial Canvas, which can be accessed through the “Classes” tab under “Learning Support” on MyWaseda. Please note that Tutorial Canvas may not function properly on PCs that do not meet the system requirements.
The course is designed for students who fit one or more of the following descriptions:
・TOEFL iBT（Speaking）score: 4 to 4.5 *taken on/before Jan 20, 2026: 20 to 24
・TOEIC S&W（Speaking）score: 160 to 179
・Who are aiming to communicate fluently and spontaneously
・Who are aiming to express ideas logically and precisely when discussing complex subjects
・Who are aiming to sustain English proficiency after coming back from studying abroad
・Who are aiming to improve English skill for working in an international field in the future
【Levels】
Students are placed in levels and grouped into classes based on the results of the LANGX Test, which is taken during a specified period. The 4 levels are Basic, Intermediate, Upper Intermediate, and Advanced. The first three (Basic, Intermediate, and Upper Intermediate) are completed in four quarters A, B, C and D, which should be taken consecutively.
・Advanced is completed in two quarters, A and B, which should be taken consecutively.
It is recommended that students begin the course in spring semester, taking A and B consecutively. Then during the fall semester registration period, students should register for C and D.
For students taking the course as an elective:
Students select the level of the course, which cannot be changed after registration. The LANGX test must be taken from the class registration screen at this time. Students can only register for A or C during the 1st registration period and need to take the test during the 1st registration period. Click “入力有” under “備考欄” to take the LANGX test.
For students who are required to take the course:
Student levels are determined by their LANGX Test scores. Compulsory students must take the LANGX Test during the designated testing period.
Please see https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html (LANGX test periods)
【Schedule】
Lessons offered twice a week
A lesson is offered on Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday for the first half of the week. The other lesson will be offered on Thursday, Friday or Saturday.

schedule_plan:
The course flow below is the same for both elective and compulsory students:
1.  Pre-Course LANGX test (approximately 30 minutes)
Please take the LANGX Test during the designated period. If you do not take the test, you may not be able to enroll in the appropriate level or class.
2.  Class announcements
Information about tutors, class days, times, and locations will be posted on Tutorial Canvas. Announcements will be made in the evening on the following dates:
Winter quarter : November 16 late afternoon
3.  Class meetings
Each class has specific “Can-dos” (learning goals). To achieve the Can-dos, students will learn vocabulary and expressions and practice using them in conversations.
①
Preparation
Before each class, students must complete the Preparation activities on Tutorial Canvas (about 40–60 minutes). These activities help students think about the topic in advance and prepare to participate actively in class.
②
In class
All classes are held on campus. Students practice conversations through pair and group work, as well as role-play activities. Students are assessed on their interactions in class, which include turn-taking, active listening, and working with others. Assessment scores and feedback will be posted on Tutorial Canvas.
③
Test Unit
Units 5 and 10 are designated as Test Units:
Unit 5: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 1–4.
Unit 10: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 6–9.
The lesson flow in Test Units is similar to regular units, but students will be specifically evaluated on whether they can use the target Can-dos correctly and effectively.
④
Final Review Sheet
After the quarter, students will receive a Final Review Sheet from each tutor. It will include comments on the student’s progress and strengths, along with advice for future study.
⑤
LANGX (Post-Course)　(approx. 30 minutes)
After Unit 10, students are required to take the LANGX test again to assess their progress.
The following are the topics for each unit.
Unit 1 Dramatic Plots
Unit 2 Expressing Reactions to Creative Works
Unit 3 Compensation
Unit 4 Expanding and Supporting Ideas
Unit 5 Test Unit (Unit 1-4)
Unit 6 Social Issues
Unit 7 Compromising
Unit 8 Developing Arguments
Unit 9 Being Diplomatic
Unit 10 Test Unit (Unit 6-9)

summary:
This course aims to develop students’ English communicative ability. Classes are small, with a maximum of 4 students, and meet on campus twice a week for 5 weeks. For details, please refer to the Guide to Tutorial English A–D ＜Quarter Course＞(hereinafter “the Student Guide”).
https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html
【Course profile】
・Each class has a maximum of 4 students.
・Lessons are offered twice a week (Saturday intensives are offered once a week, 2 periods in a row).
・Schedules differ between campuses, and each section is held only on one campus. Once course registration is complete, it cannot be changed.
・The course uses Tutorial Canvas, which can be accessed through the “Classes” tab under “Learning Support” on MyWaseda. Please note that Tutorial Canvas may not function properly on PCs that do not meet the system requirements.
The course is designed for students who fit one or more of the following descriptions:
・TOEFL iBT（Speaking）score: 4 to 4.5 *taken on/before Jan 20, 2026: 20 to 24
・TOEIC S&W（Speaking）score: 160 to 179
・Who are aiming to communicate fluently and spontaneously
・Who are aiming to express ideas logically and precisely when discussing complex subjects
・Who are aiming to sustain English proficiency after coming back from studying abroad
・Who are aiming to improve English skill for working in an international field in the future
【Levels】
Students are placed in levels and grouped into classes based on the results of the LANGX Test, which is taken during a specified period. The 4 levels are Basic, Intermediate, Upper Intermediate, and Advanced. The first three (Basic, Intermediate, and Upper Intermediate) are completed in four quarters A, B, C and D, which should be taken consecutively.
・Advanced is completed in two quarters, A and B, which should be taken consecutively.
It is recommended that students begin the course in spring semester, taking A and B consecutively. Then during the fall semester registration period, students should register for C and D.
For students taking the course as an elective:
Students select the level of the course, which cannot be changed after registration. The LANGX test must be taken from the class registration screen at this time. Students can only register for A or C during the 1st registration period and need to take the test during the 1st registration period. Click “入力有” under “備考欄” to take the LANGX test.
For students who are required to take the course:
Student levels are determined by their LANGX Test scores. Compulsory students must take the LANGX Test during the designated testing period.
Please see https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html (LANGX test periods)
【Schedule】
Lessons offered twice a week
A lesson is offered on Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday for the first half of the week. The other lesson will be offered on Thursday, Friday or Saturday.

goal: Students will be able to understand the main ideas of the wide-ranging and complex subjects, use appropriate language, and express their thoughts fluently and logically.

schedule_plan:
The course flow below is the same for both elective and compulsory students:
1.  Pre-Course LANGX test (approximately 30 minutes)
Please take the LANGX Test during the designated period. If you do not take the test, you may not be able to enroll in the appropriate level or class.
2.  Class announcements
Information about tutors, class days, times, and locations will be posted on Tutorial Canvas. Announcements will be made in the evening on the following dates:
Winter quarter : November 16 late afternoon
3.  Class meetings
Each class has specific “Can-dos” (learning goals). To achieve the Can-dos, students will learn vocabulary and expressions and practice using them in conversations.
①
Preparation
Before each class, students must complete the Preparation activities on Tutorial Canvas (about 40–60 minutes). These activities help students think about the topic in advance and prepare to participate actively in class.
②
In class
All classes are held on campus. Students practice conversations through pair and group work, as well as role-play activities. Students are assessed on their interactions in class, which include turn-taking, active listening, and working with others. Assessment scores and feedback will be posted on Tutorial Canvas.
③
Test Unit
Units 5 and 10 are designated as Test Units:
Unit 5: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 1–4.
Unit 10: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 6–9.
The lesson flow in Test Units is similar to regular units, but students will be specifically evaluated on whether they can use the target Can-dos correctly and effectively.
④
Final Review Sheet
After the quarter, students will receive a Final Review Sheet from each tutor. It will include comments on the student’s progress and strengths, along with advice for future study.
⑤
LANGX (Post-Course)　(approx. 30 minutes)
After Unit 10, students are required to take the LANGX test again to assess their progress.
The following are the topics for each unit.
Unit 1 Dramatic Plots
Unit 2 Expressing Reactions to Creative Works
Unit 3 Compensation
Unit 4 Expanding and Supporting Ideas
Unit 5 Test Unit (Unit 1-4)
Unit 6 Social Issues
Unit 7 Compromising
Unit 8 Developing Arguments
Unit 9 Being Diplomatic
Unit 10 Test Unit (Unit 6-9)

summary:
This course aims to develop students’ English communicative ability. Classes are small, with a maximum of 4 students, and meet on campus twice a week for 5 weeks. For details, please refer to the Guide to Tutorial English A–D ＜Quarter Course＞(hereinafter “the Student Guide”).
https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html
【Course profile】
・Each class has a maximum of 4 students.
・Lessons are offered twice a week (Saturday intensives are offered once a week, 2 periods in a row).
・Schedules differ between campuses, and each section is held only on one campus. Once course registration is complete, it cannot be changed.
・The course uses Tutorial Canvas, which can be accessed through the “Classes” tab under “Learning Support” on MyWaseda. Please note that Tutorial Canvas may not function properly on PCs that do not meet the system requirements.
The course is designed for students who fit one or more of the following descriptions:
・TOEFL iBT（Speaking）score: 4 to 4.5 *taken on/before Jan 20, 2026: 20 to 24
・TOEIC S&W（Speaking）score: 160 to 179
・Who are aiming to communicate fluently and spontaneously
・Who are aiming to express ideas logically and precisely when discussing complex subjects
・Who are aiming to sustain English proficiency after coming back from studying abroad
・Who are aiming to improve English skill for working in an international field in the future
【Levels】
Students are placed in levels and grouped into classes based on the results of the LANGX Test, which is taken during a specified period. The 4 levels are Basic, Intermediate, Upper Intermediate, and Advanced. The first three (Basic, Intermediate, and Upper Intermediate) are completed in four quarters A, B, C and D, which should be taken consecutively.
・Advanced is completed in two quarters, A and B, which should be taken consecutively.
It is recommended that students begin the course in spring semester, taking A and B consecutively. Then during the fall semester registration period, students should register for C and D.
For students taking the course as an elective:
Students select the level of the course, which cannot be changed after registration. The LANGX test must be taken from the class registration screen at this time. Students can only register for A or C during the 1st registration period and need to take the test during the 1st registration period. Click “入力有” under “備考欄” to take the LANGX test.
For students who are required to take the course:
Student levels are determined by their LANGX Test scores. Compulsory students must take the LANGX Test during the designated testing period.
Please see https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html (LANGX test periods)
【Schedule】
Lessons offered twice a week
A lesson is offered on Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday for the first half of the week. The other lesson will be offered on Thursday, Friday or Saturday.

schedule_plan:
The course flow below is the same for both elective and compulsory students:
1.  Pre-Course LANGX test (approximately 30 minutes)
Please take the LANGX Test during the designated period. If you do not take the test, you may not be able to enroll in the appropriate level or class.
2.  Class announcements
Information about tutors, class days, times, and locations will be posted on Tutorial Canvas. Announcements will be made in the evening on the following dates:
Winter quarter : November 16 late afternoon
3.  Class meetings
Each class has specific “Can-dos” (learning goals). To achieve the Can-dos, students will learn vocabulary and expressions and practice using them in conversations.
①
Preparation
Before each class, students must complete the Preparation activities on Tutorial Canvas (about 40–60 minutes). These activities help students think about the topic in advance and prepare to participate actively in class.
②
In class
All classes are held on campus. Students practice conversations through pair and group work, as well as role-play activities. Students are assessed on their interactions in class, which include turn-taking, active listening, and working with others. Assessment scores and feedback will be posted on Tutorial Canvas.
③
Test Unit
Units 5 and 10 are designated as Test Units:
Unit 5: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 1–4.
Unit 10: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 6–9.
The lesson flow in Test Units is similar to regular units, but students will be specifically evaluated on whether they can use the target Can-dos correctly and effectively.
④
Final Review Sheet
After the quarter, students will receive a Final Review Sheet from each tutor. It will include comments on the student’s progress and strengths, along with advice for future study.
⑤
LANGX (Post-Course)　(approx. 30 minutes)
After Unit 10, students are required to take the LANGX test again to assess their progress.
The following are the topics for each unit.
Unit 1 Dramatic Plots
Unit 2 Expressing Reactions to Creative Works
Unit 3 Compensation
Unit 4 Expanding and Supporting Ideas
Unit 5 Test Unit (Unit 1-4)
Unit 6 Social Issues
Unit 7 Compromising
Unit 8 Developing Arguments
Unit 9 Being Diplomatic
Unit 10 Test Unit (Unit 6-9)

Unit 4 Expanding and Supporting Ideas
Unit 5 Test Unit (Unit 1-4)

summary:
This course aims to develop students’ English communicative ability. Classes are small, with a maximum of 4 students, and meet on campus twice a week for 5 weeks. For details, please refer to the Guide to Tutorial English A–D ＜Quarter Course＞(hereinafter “the Student Guide”).
https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html
【Course profile】
・Each class has a maximum of 4 students.
・Lessons are offered twice a week (Saturday intensives are offered once a week, 2 periods in a row).
・Schedules differ between campuses, and each section is held only on one campus. Once course registration is complete, it cannot be changed.
・The course uses Tutorial Canvas, which can be accessed through the “Classes” tab under “Learning Support” on MyWaseda. Please note that Tutorial Canvas may not function properly on PCs that do not meet the system requirements.
The course is designed for students who fit one or more of the following descriptions:
・TOEFL iBT（Speaking）score: 4 to 4.5 *taken on/before Jan 20, 2026: 20 to 24
・TOEIC S&W（Speaking）score: 160 to 179
・Who are aiming to communicate fluently and spontaneously
・Who are aiming to express ideas logically and precisely when discussing complex subjects
・Who are aiming to sustain English proficiency after coming back from studying abroad
・Who are aiming to improve English skill for working in an international field in the future
【Levels】
Students are placed in levels and grouped into classes based on the results of the LANGX Test, which is taken during a specified period. The 4 levels are Basic, Intermediate, Upper Intermediate, and Advanced. The first three (Basic, Intermediate, and Upper Intermediate) are completed in four quarters A, B, C and D, which should be taken consecutively.
・Advanced is completed in two quarters, A and B, which should be taken consecutively.
It is recommended that students begin the course in spring semester, taking A and B consecutively. Then during the fall semester registration period, students should register for C and D.
For students taking the course as an elective:
Students select the level of the course, which cannot be changed after registration. The LANGX test must be taken from the class registration screen at this time. Students can only register for A or C during the 1st registration period and need to take the test during the 1st registration period. Click “入力有” under “備考欄” to take the LANGX test.
For students who are required to take the course:
Student levels are determined by their LANGX Test scores. Compulsory students must take the LANGX Test during the designated testing period.
Please see https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html (LANGX test periods)
【Schedule】
Lessons offered twice a week
A lesson is offered on Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday for the first half of the week. The other lesson will be offered on Thursday, Friday or Saturday.

schedule_plan:
The course flow below is the same for both elective and compulsory students:
1.  Pre-Course LANGX test (approximately 30 minutes)
Please take the LANGX Test during the designated period. If you do not take the test, you may not be able to enroll in the appropriate level or class.
2.  Class announcements
Information about tutors, class days, times, and locations will be posted on Tutorial Canvas. Announcements will be made in the evening on the following dates:
Winter quarter : November 16 late afternoon
3.  Class meetings
Each class has specific “Can-dos” (learning goals). To achieve the Can-dos, students will learn vocabulary and expressions and practice using them in conversations.
①
Preparation
Before each class, students must complete the Preparation activities on Tutorial Canvas (about 40–60 minutes). These activities help students think about the topic in advance and prepare to participate actively in class.
②
In class
All classes are held on campus. Students practice conversations through pair and group work, as well as role-play activities. Students are assessed on their interactions in class, which include turn-taking, active listening, and working with others. Assessment scores and feedback will be posted on Tutorial Canvas.
③
Test Unit
Units 5 and 10 are designated as Test Units:
Unit 5: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 1–4.
Unit 10: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 6–9.
The lesson flow in Test Units is similar to regular units, but students will be specifically evaluated on whether they can use the target Can-dos correctly and effectively.
④
Final Review Sheet
After the quarter, students will receive a Final Review Sheet from each tutor. It will include comments on the student’s progress and strengths, along with advice for future study.
⑤
LANGX (Post-Course)　(approx. 30 minutes)
After Unit 10, students are required to take the LANGX test again to assess their progress.
The following are the topics for each unit.
Unit 1 Dramatic Plots
Unit 2 Expressing Reactions to Creative Works
Unit 3 Compensation
Unit 4 Expanding and Supporting Ideas
Unit 5 Test Unit (Unit 1-4)
Unit 6 Social Issues
Unit 7 Compromising
Unit 8 Developing Arguments
Unit 9 Being Diplomatic
Unit 10 Test Unit (Unit 6-9)

Students select the level of the course, which cannot be changed after registration. The LANGX test must be taken from the class registration screen at this time. Students can only register for A or C during the 1st registration period and need to take the test during the 1st registration period. Click “入力有” under “備考欄” to take the LANGX test.

Preparation

②
In class

Students are assessed on their interactions in class, which include turn-taking, active listening, and working with others. Assessment scores and feedback will be posted on Tutorial Canvas.
③
Test Unit

Unit 5: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 1–4.
Unit 10: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 6–9.

LANGX (Post-Course)　(approx. 30 minutes)
After Unit 10, students are required to take the LANGX test again to assess their progress.

Unit 1 Dramatic Plots
Unit 2 Expressing Reactions to Creative Works
Unit 3 Compensation
Unit 4 Expanding and Supporting Ideas
Unit 5 Test Unit (Unit 1-4)
Unit 6 Social Issues
Unit 7 Compromising
Unit 8 Developing Arguments
Unit 9 Being Diplomatic
Unit 10 Test Unit (Unit 6-9)

summary:
This course aims to develop students’ English communicative ability. Classes are small, with a maximum of 4 students, and meet on campus twice a week for 5 weeks. For details, please refer to the Guide to Tutorial English A–D ＜Quarter Course＞(hereinafter “the Student Guide”).
https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html
【Course profile】
・Each class has a maximum of 4 students.
・Lessons are offered twice a week (Saturday intensives are offered once a week, 2 periods in a row).
・Schedules differ between campuses, and each section is held only on one campus. Once course registration is complete, it cannot be changed.
・The course uses Tutorial Canvas, which can be accessed through the “Classes” tab under “Learning Support” on MyWaseda. Please note that Tutorial Canvas may not function properly on PCs that do not meet the system requirements.
The course is designed for students who fit one or more of the following descriptions:
・TOEFL iBT（Speaking）score: 4 to 4.5 *taken on/before Jan 20, 2026: 20 to 24
・TOEIC S&W（Speaking）score: 160 to 179
・Who are aiming to communicate fluently and spontaneously
・Who are aiming to express ideas logically and precisely when discussing complex subjects
・Who are aiming to sustain English proficiency after coming back from studying abroad
・Who are aiming to improve English skill for working in an international field in the future
【Levels】
Students are placed in levels and grouped into classes based on the results of the LANGX Test, which is taken during a specified period. The 4 levels are Basic, Intermediate, Upper Intermediate, and Advanced. The first three (Basic, Intermediate, and Upper Intermediate) are completed in four quarters A, B, C and D, which should be taken consecutively.
・Advanced is completed in two quarters, A and B, which should be taken consecutively.
It is recommended that students begin the course in spring semester, taking A and B consecutively. Then during the fall semester registration period, students should register for C and D.
For students taking the course as an elective:
Students select the level of the course, which cannot be changed after registration. The LANGX test must be taken from the class registration screen at this time. Students can only register for A or C during the 1st registration period and need to take the test during the 1st registration period. Click “入力有” under “備考欄” to take the LANGX test.
For students who are required to take the course:
Student levels are determined by their LANGX Test scores. Compulsory students must take the LANGX Test during the designated testing period.
Please see https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html (LANGX test periods)
【Schedule】
Lessons offered twice a week
A lesson is offered on Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday for the first half of the week. The other lesson will be offered on Thursday, Friday or Saturday.

schedule_plan:
The course flow below is the same for both elective and compulsory students:
1.  Pre-Course LANGX test (approximately 30 minutes)
Please take the LANGX Test during the designated period. If you do not take the test, you may not be able to enroll in the appropriate level or class.
2.  Class announcements
Information about tutors, class days, times, and locations will be posted on Tutorial Canvas. Announcements will be made in the evening on the following dates:
Winter quarter : November 16 late afternoon
3.  Class meetings
Each class has specific “Can-dos” (learning goals). To achieve the Can-dos, students will learn vocabulary and expressions and practice using them in conversations.
①
Preparation
Before each class, students must complete the Preparation activities on Tutorial Canvas (about 40–60 minutes). These activities help students think about the topic in advance and prepare to participate actively in class.
②
In class
All classes are held on campus. Students practice conversations through pair and group work, as well as role-play activities. Students are assessed on their interactions in class, which include turn-taking, active listening, and working with others. Assessment scores and feedback will be posted on Tutorial Canvas.
③
Test Unit
Units 5 and 10 are designated as Test Units:
Unit 5: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 1–4.
Unit 10: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 6–9.
The lesson flow in Test Units is similar to regular units, but students will be specifically evaluated on whether they can use the target Can-dos correctly and effectively.
④
Final Review Sheet
After the quarter, students will receive a Final Review Sheet from each tutor. It will include comments on the student’s progress and strengths, along with advice for future study.
⑤
LANGX (Post-Course)　(approx. 30 minutes)
After Unit 10, students are required to take the LANGX test again to assess their progress.
The following are the topics for each unit.
Unit 1 Dramatic Plots
Unit 2 Expressing Reactions to Creative Works
Unit 3 Compensation
Unit 4 Expanding and Supporting Ideas
Unit 5 Test Unit (Unit 1-4)
Unit 6 Social Issues
Unit 7 Compromising
Unit 8 Developing Arguments
Unit 9 Being Diplomatic
Unit 10 Test Unit (Unit 6-9)

・Who are aiming to express ideas logically and precisely when discussing complex subjects
・Who are aiming to sustain English proficiency after coming back from studying abroad

Students select the level of the course, which cannot be changed after registration. The LANGX test must be taken from the class registration screen at this time. Students can only register for A or C during the 1st registration period and need to take the test during the 1st registration period. Click “入力有” under “備考欄” to take the LANGX test.

Preparation

②
In class

Students are assessed on their interactions in class, which include turn-taking, active listening, and working with others. Assessment scores and feedback will be posted on Tutorial Canvas.
③
Test Unit

Unit 5: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 1–4.
Unit 10: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 6–9.

LANGX (Post-Course)　(approx. 30 minutes)
After Unit 10, students are required to take the LANGX test again to assess their progress.

Unit 1 Dramatic Plots
Unit 2 Expressing Reactions to Creative Works
Unit 3 Compensation
Unit 4 Expanding and Supporting Ideas
Unit 5 Test Unit (Unit 1-4)
Unit 6 Social Issues
Unit 7 Compromising
Unit 8 Developing Arguments
Unit 9 Being Diplomatic
Unit 10 Test Unit (Unit 6-9)

This course aims to develop students’ English communicative ability. Classes are small, with a maximum of 4 students, and meet on campus twice a week for 5 weeks. For details, please refer to the Guide to Tutorial English A–D ＜Quarter Course＞(hereinafter “the Student Guide”).
https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html
【Course profile】
・Each class has a maximum of 4 students.
・Lessons are offered twice a week (Saturday intensives are offered once a week, 2 periods in a row).
・Schedules differ between campuses, and each section is held only on one campus. Once course registration is complete, it cannot be changed.
・The course uses Tutorial Canvas, which can be accessed through the “Classes” tab under “Learning Support” on MyWaseda. Please note that Tutorial Canvas may not function properly on PCs that do not meet the system requirements.
The course is designed for students who fit one or more of the following descriptions:
・TOEFL iBT（Speaking）score: above 5  *taken on/before Jan 20, 2026: above 25
・TOEIC S&W（Speaking）score: above 180
・Who are aiming to understand and speak English at a fast, native pace on any subject, recognizing implicit meaning and the nuances of the words
【Levels】
Students are placed in levels and grouped into classes based on the results of the LANGX Test, which is taken during a specified period. The 4 levels are Basic, Intermediate, Upper Intermediate, and Advanced. The first three (Basic, Intermediate, and Upper Intermediate) are completed in four quarters A, B, C and D, which should be taken consecutively.
・Advanced is completed in two quarters, A and B, which should be taken consecutively.
It is recommended that students begin the course in spring semester or fall semester, taking A and B consecutively.
For students taking the course as an elective:
Students select the level of the course, which cannot be changed after registration. The LANGX test must be taken from the class registration screen at this time. Students can only register for A or C during the 1st registration period and need to take the test during the 1st registration period. Click “入力有” under “備考欄” to take the LANGX test.
For students who are required to take the course:
Student levels are determined by their LANGX Test scores. Compulsory students must take the LANGX Test during the designated testing period.
Please see https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html (LANGX test periods)
【Schedule】
Lessons offered twice a week
A lesson is offered on Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday for the first half of the week. The other lesson will be offered on Thursday, Friday or Saturday.

schedule_plan:
The course flow below is the same for both elective and compulsory students:
1.  Pre-Course LANGX test (approximately 30 minutes)
Please take the LANGX Test during the designated period. If you do not take the test, you may not be able to enroll in the appropriate level or class.
2.  Class announcements
Information about tutors, class days, times, and locations will be posted on Tutorial Canvas. Announcements will be made in the evening on the following dates:
Spring quarter: April 15 late afternoon
Fall quarter: October 1 late afternoon
3.  Class meetings
Each class has specific “Can-dos” (learning goals). To achieve the Can-dos, students will learn vocabulary and expressions and practice using them in conversations.
①
Preparation
Before each class, students must complete the Preparation activities on Tutorial Canvas (about 40–60 minutes). These activities help students think about the topic in advance and prepare to participate actively in class.
②
In class
All classes are held on campus. Students practice conversations through pair and group work, as well as role-play activities. Students are assessed on their interactions in class, which include turn-taking, active listening, and working with others. Assessment scores and feedback will be posted on Tutorial Canvas.
③
Test Unit
Units 5 and 10 are designated as Test Units:
Unit 5: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 1–4.
Unit 10: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 6–9.
The lesson flow in Test Units is similar to regular units, but students will be specifically evaluated on whether they can use the target Can-dos correctly and effectively.
④
Final Review Sheet
After the quarter, students will receive a Final Review Sheet from each tutor. It will include comments on the student’s progress and strengths, along with advice for future study.
⑤
LANGX (Post-Course)　(approx. 30 minutes)
After Unit 10, students are required to take the LANGX test again to assess their progress.
The following are the topics for each unit.
Unit 1 Working with Others (1)
Unit 2 Working with Others (2)
Unit 3 Health and Fitness (1)
Unit 4 Health and Fitness (2)
Unit 5 Test Unit (Unit 1-4)
Unit 6 Complex Issues (1)
Unit 7 Complex Issues (2)
Unit 8 Education (1)
Unit 9 Education (2)
Unit 10 Test Unit (Unit 6-9)

Preparation

https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html
【Course profile】
・Each class has a maximum of 4 students.
・Lessons are offered twice a week (Saturday intensives are offered once a week, 2 periods in a row).
・Schedules differ between campuses, and each section is held only on one campus. Once course registration is complete, it cannot be changed.
・The course uses Tutorial Canvas, which can be accessed through the “Classes” tab under “Learning Support” on MyWaseda. Please note that Tutorial Canvas may not function properly on PCs that do not meet the system requirements.
The course is designed for students who fit one or more of the following descriptions:
・TOEFL iBT（Speaking）score: above 5  *taken on/before Jan 20, 2026: above 25
・TOEIC S&W（Speaking）score: above 180
・Who are aiming to understand and speak English at a fast, native pace on any subject, recognizing implicit meaning and the nuances of the words
【Levels】
Students are placed in levels and grouped into classes based on the results of the LANGX Test, which is taken during a specified period. The 4 levels are Basic, Intermediate, Upper Intermediate, and Advanced. The first three (Basic, Intermediate, and Upper Intermediate) are completed in four quarters A, B, C and D, which should be taken consecutively.
・Advanced is completed in two quarters, A and B, which should be taken consecutively.
It is recommended that students begin the course in spring semester or fall semester, taking A and B consecutively.
For students taking the course as an elective:
Students select the level of the course, which cannot be changed after registration. The LANGX test must be taken from the class registration screen at this time. Students can only register for A or C during the 1st registration period and need to take the test during the 1st registration period. Click “入力有” under “備考欄” to take the LANGX test.
For students who are required to take the course:
Student levels are determined by their LANGX Test scores. Compulsory students must take the LANGX Test during the designated testing period.
Please see https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html (LANGX test periods)

This course aims to develop students’ English communicative ability. Classes are small, with a maximum of 4 students, and meet on campus twice a week for 5 weeks. For details, please refer to the Guide to Tutorial English A–D ＜Quarter Course＞(hereinafter “the Student Guide”).
https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html
【Course profile】
・Each class has a maximum of 4 students.
・Lessons are offered twice a week (Saturday intensives are offered once a week, 2 periods in a row).
・Schedules differ between campuses, and each section is held only on one campus. Once course registration is complete, it cannot be changed.
・The course uses Tutorial Canvas, which can be accessed through the “Classes” tab under “Learning Support” on MyWaseda. Please note that Tutorial Canvas may not function properly on PCs that do not meet the system requirements.
The course is designed for students who fit one or more of the following descriptions:
・TOEFL iBT（Speaking）score: above 5  *taken on/before Jan 20, 2026: above 25
・TOEIC S&W（Speaking）score: above 180
・Who are aiming to understand and speak English at a fast, native pace on any subject, recognizing implicit meaning and the nuances of the words
【Levels】
Students are placed in levels and grouped into classes based on the results of the LANGX Test, which is taken during a specified period. The 4 levels are Basic, Intermediate, Upper Intermediate, and Advanced. The first three (Basic, Intermediate, and Upper Intermediate) are completed in four quarters A, B, C and D, which should be taken consecutively.
・Advanced is completed in two quarters, A and B, which should be taken consecutively.
It is recommended that students begin the course in spring semester or fall semester, taking A and B consecutively.
For students taking the course as an elective:
Students select the level of the course, which cannot be changed after registration. The LANGX test must be taken from the class registration screen at this time. Students can only register for A or C during the 1st registration period and need to take the test during the 1st registration period. Click “入力有” under “備考欄” to take the LANGX test.
For students who are required to take the course:
Student levels are determined by their LANGX Test scores. Compulsory students must take the LANGX Test during the designated testing period.
Please see https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html (LANGX test periods)
【Schedule】
Lessons offered twice a week
A lesson is offered on Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday for the first half of the week. The other lesson will be offered on Thursday, Friday or Saturday.

schedule_plan:
The course flow below is the same for both elective and compulsory students:
1.  Pre-Course LANGX test (approximately 30 minutes)
Please take the LANGX Test during the designated period. If you do not take the test, you may not be able to enroll in the appropriate level or class.
2.  Class announcements
Information about tutors, class days, times, and locations will be posted on Tutorial Canvas. Announcements will be made in the evening on the following dates:
Spring quarter: April 15 late afternoon
Fall quarter: October 1 late afternoon
3.  Class meetings
Each class has specific “Can-dos” (learning goals). To achieve the Can-dos, students will learn vocabulary and expressions and practice using them in conversations.
①
Preparation
Before each class, students must complete the Preparation activities on Tutorial Canvas (about 40–60 minutes). These activities help students think about the topic in advance and prepare to participate actively in class.
②
In class
All classes are held on campus. Students practice conversations through pair and group work, as well as role-play activities. Students are assessed on their interactions in class, which include turn-taking, active listening, and working with others. Assessment scores and feedback will be posted on Tutorial Canvas.
③
Test Unit
Units 5 and 10 are designated as Test Units:
Unit 5: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 1–4.
Unit 10: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 6–9.
The lesson flow in Test Units is similar to regular units, but students will be specifically evaluated on whether they can use the target Can-dos correctly and effectively.
④
Final Review Sheet
After the quarter, students will receive a Final Review Sheet from each tutor. It will include comments on the student’s progress and strengths, along with advice for future study.
⑤
LANGX (Post-Course)　(approx. 30 minutes)
After Unit 10, students are required to take the LANGX test again to assess their progress.
The following are the topics for each unit.
Unit 1 Working with Others (1)
Unit 2 Working with Others (2)
Unit 3 Health and Fitness (1)
Unit 4 Health and Fitness (2)
Unit 5 Test Unit (Unit 1-4)
Unit 6 Complex Issues (1)
Unit 7 Complex Issues (2)
Unit 8 Education (1)
Unit 9 Education (2)
Unit 10 Test Unit (Unit 6-9)

【Course profile】
・Each class has a maximum of 4 students.
・Lessons are offered twice a week (Saturday intensives are offered once a week, 2 periods in a row).
・Schedules differ between campuses, and each section is held only on one campus. Once course registration is complete, it cannot be changed.
・The course uses Tutorial Canvas, which can be accessed through the “Classes” tab under “Learning Support” on MyWaseda. Please note that Tutorial Canvas may not function properly on PCs that do not meet the system requirements.
The course is designed for students who fit one or more of the following descriptions:
・TOEFL iBT（Speaking）score: above 5  *taken on/before Jan 20, 2026: above 25
・TOEIC S&W（Speaking）score: above 180
・Who are aiming to understand and speak English at a fast, native pace on any subject, recognizing implicit meaning and the nuances of the words
【Levels】
Students are placed in levels and grouped into classes based on the results of the LANGX Test, which is taken during a specified period. The 4 levels are Basic, Intermediate, Upper Intermediate, and Advanced. The first three (Basic, Intermediate, and Upper Intermediate) are completed in four quarters A, B, C and D, which should be taken consecutively.
・Advanced is completed in two quarters, A and B, which should be taken consecutively.
It is recommended that students begin the course in spring semester or fall semester, taking A and B consecutively.
For students taking the course as an elective:
Students select the level of the course, which cannot be changed after registration. The LANGX test must be taken from the class registration screen at this time. Students can only register for A or C during the 1st registration period and need to take the test during the 1st registration period. Click “入力有” under “備考欄” to take the LANGX test.
For students who are required to take the course:
Student levels are determined by their LANGX Test scores. Compulsory students must take the LANGX Test during the designated testing period.
Please see https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html (LANGX test periods)

This course aims to develop students’ English communicative ability. Classes are small, with a maximum of 4 students, and meet on campus twice a week for 5 weeks. For details, please refer to the Guide to Tutorial English A–D ＜Quarter Course＞(hereinafter “the Student Guide”).
https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html
【Course profile】
・Each class has a maximum of 4 students.
・Lessons are offered twice a week (Saturday intensives are offered once a week, 2 periods in a row).
・Schedules differ between campuses, and each section is held only on one campus. Once course registration is complete, it cannot be changed.
・The course uses Tutorial Canvas, which can be accessed through the “Classes” tab under “Learning Support” on MyWaseda. Please note that Tutorial Canvas may not function properly on PCs that do not meet the system requirements.
The course is designed for students who fit one or more of the following descriptions:
・TOEFL iBT（Speaking）score: above 5  *taken on/before Jan 20, 2026: above 25
・TOEIC S&W（Speaking）score: above 180
・Who are aiming to understand and speak English at a fast, native pace on any subject, recognizing implicit meaning and the nuances of the words
【Levels】
Students are placed in levels and grouped into classes based on the results of the LANGX Test, which is taken during a specified period. The 4 levels are Basic, Intermediate, Upper Intermediate, and Advanced. The first three (Basic, Intermediate, and Upper Intermediate) are completed in four quarters A, B, C and D, which should be taken consecutively.
・Advanced is completed in two quarters, A and B, which should be taken consecutively.
It is recommended that students begin the course in spring semester or fall semester, taking A and B consecutively.
For students taking the course as an elective:
Students select the level of the course, which cannot be changed after registration. The LANGX test must be taken from the class registration screen at this time. Students can only register for A or C during the 1st registration period and need to take the test during the 1st registration period. Click “入力有” under “備考欄” to take the LANGX test.
For students who are required to take the course:
Student levels are determined by their LANGX Test scores. Compulsory students must take the LANGX Test during the designated testing period.
Please see https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html (LANGX test periods)
【Schedule】
Lessons offered twice a week
A lesson is offered on Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday for the first half of the week. The other lesson will be offered on Thursday, Friday or Saturday.

schedule_plan:
The course flow below is the same for both elective and compulsory students:
1.  Pre-Course LANGX test (approximately 30 minutes)
Please take the LANGX Test during the designated period. If you do not take the test, you may not be able to enroll in the appropriate level or class.
2.  Class announcements
Information about tutors, class days, times, and locations will be posted on Tutorial Canvas. Announcements will be made in the evening on the following dates:
Spring quarter: April 15 late afternoon
Fall quarter: October 1 late afternoon
3.  Class meetings
Each class has specific “Can-dos” (learning goals). To achieve the Can-dos, students will learn vocabulary and expressions and practice using them in conversations.
①
Preparation
Before each class, students must complete the Preparation activities on Tutorial Canvas (about 40–60 minutes). These activities help students think about the topic in advance and prepare to participate actively in class.
②
In class
All classes are held on campus. Students practice conversations through pair and group work, as well as role-play activities. Students are assessed on their interactions in class, which include turn-taking, active listening, and working with others. Assessment scores and feedback will be posted on Tutorial Canvas.
③
Test Unit
Units 5 and 10 are designated as Test Units:
Unit 5: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 1–4.
Unit 10: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 6–9.
The lesson flow in Test Units is similar to regular units, but students will be specifically evaluated on whether they can use the target Can-dos correctly and effectively.
④
Final Review Sheet
After the quarter, students will receive a Final Review Sheet from each tutor. It will include comments on the student’s progress and strengths, along with advice for future study.
⑤
LANGX (Post-Course)　(approx. 30 minutes)
After Unit 10, students are required to take the LANGX test again to assess their progress.
The following are the topics for each unit.
Unit 1 Working with Others (1)
Unit 2 Working with Others (2)
Unit 3 Health and Fitness (1)
Unit 4 Health and Fitness (2)
Unit 5 Test Unit (Unit 1-4)
Unit 6 Complex Issues (1)
Unit 7 Complex Issues (2)
Unit 8 Education (1)
Unit 9 Education (2)
Unit 10 Test Unit (Unit 6-9)

・TOEFL iBT（Speaking）score: above 5  *taken on/before Jan 20, 2026: above 25
・TOEIC S&W（Speaking）score: above 180
・Who are aiming to understand and speak English at a fast, native pace on any subject, recognizing implicit meaning and the nuances of the words

The first three (Basic, Intermediate, and Upper Intermediate) are completed in four quarters A, B, C and D, which should be taken consecutively.
・Advanced is completed in two quarters, A and B, which should be taken consecutively.
It is recommended that students begin the course in spring semester or fall semester, taking A and B consecutively.
For students taking the course as an elective:
Students select the level of the course, which cannot be changed after registration. The LANGX test must be taken from the class registration screen at this time. Students can only register for A or C during the 1st registration period and need to take the test during the 1st registration period. Click “入力有” under “備考欄” to take the LANGX test.

Please see https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html (LANGX test periods)

Preparation

In class

Unit 5: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 1–4.

Unit 5 Test Unit (Unit 1-4)

Unit 7 Complex Issues (2)
Unit 8 Science and Technology (1)

summary:
This course aims to develop students’ English communicative ability. Classes are small, with a maximum of 4 students, and meet on campus twice a week for 5 weeks. For details, please refer to the Guide to Tutorial English A–D ＜Quarter Course＞(hereinafter “the Student Guide”).
https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html
【Course profile】
・Each class has a maximum of 4 students.
・Lessons are offered twice a week (Saturday intensives are offered once a week, 2 periods in a row).
・Schedules differ between campuses, and each section is held only on one campus. Once course registration is complete, it cannot be changed.
・The course uses Tutorial Canvas, which can be accessed through the “Classes” tab under “Learning Support” on MyWaseda. Please note that Tutorial Canvas may not function properly on PCs that do not meet the system requirements.
The course is designed for students who fit one or more of the following descriptions:
・TOEFL iBT（Speaking）score: above 5  *taken on/before Jan 20, 2026: above 25
・TOEIC S&W（Speaking）score: above 180
・Who are aiming to understand and speak English at a fast, native pace on any subject, recognizing implicit meaning and the nuances of the words
【Levels】
Students are placed in levels and grouped into classes based on the results of the LANGX Test, which is taken during a specified period. The 4 levels are Basic, Intermediate, Upper Intermediate, and Advanced. The first three (Basic, Intermediate, and Upper Intermediate) are completed in four quarters A, B, C and D, which should be taken consecutively.
・Advanced is completed in two quarters, A and B, which should be taken consecutively.
It is recommended that students begin the course in spring semester or fall semester, taking A and B consecutively.
For students taking the course as an elective:
Students select the level of the course, which cannot be changed after registration. The LANGX test must be taken from the class registration screen at this time. Students can only register for A or C during the 1st registration period and need to take the test during the 1st registration period. Click “入力有” under “備考欄” to take the LANGX test.
For students who are required to take the course:
Student levels are determined by their LANGX Test scores. Compulsory students must take the LANGX Test during the designated testing period.
Please see https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html (LANGX test periods)
【Schedule】
Lessons offered twice a week
A lesson is offered on Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday for the first half of the week. The other lesson will be offered on Thursday, Friday or Saturday.

schedule_plan:
The course flow below is the same for both elective and compulsory students:
1.  Pre-Course LANGX test (approximately 30 minutes)
Please take the LANGX Test during the designated period. If you do not take the test, you may not be able to enroll in the appropriate level or class.
2.  Class announcements
Information about tutors, class days, times, and locations will be posted on Tutorial Canvas. Announcements will be made in the evening on the following dates:
Summer quarter: June 1 late afternoon
Winter quarter : November 16 late afternoon
3.  Class meetings
Each class has specific “Can-dos” (learning goals). To achieve the Can-dos, students will learn vocabulary and expressions and practice using them in conversations.
①
Preparation
Before each class, students must complete the Preparation activities on Tutorial Canvas (about 40–60 minutes). These activities help students think about the topic in advance and prepare to participate actively in class.
②
In class
All classes are held on campus. Students practice conversations through pair and group work, as well as role-play activities. Students are assessed on their interactions in class, which include turn-taking, active listening, and working with others. Assessment scores and feedback will be posted on Tutorial Canvas.
③
Test Unit
Units 5 and 10 are designated as Test Units:
Unit 5: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 1–4.
Unit 10: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 6–9.
The lesson flow in Test Units is similar to regular units, but students will be specifically evaluated on whether they can use the target Can-dos correctly and effectively.
④
Final Review Sheet
After the quarter, students will receive a Final Review Sheet from each tutor. It will include comments on the student’s progress and strengths, along with advice for future study.
⑤
LANGX (Post-Course)　(approx. 30 minutes)
After Unit 10, students are required to take the LANGX test again to assess their progress.
The following are the topics for each unit.
Unit 1 Culture (1)
Unit 2 Culture (2)
Unit 3 Social Issues (1)
Unit 4 Social Issues (2)
Unit 5 Test Unit (Unit 1-4)
Unit 6 Complex Issues (1)
Unit 7 Complex Issues (2)
Unit 8 Science and Technology (1)
Unit 9 Science and Technology (2)
Unit 10 Test Unit (Unit 6-9)

This course aims to develop students’ English communicative ability. Classes are small, with a maximum of 4 students, and meet on campus twice a week for 5 weeks. For details, please refer to the Guide to Tutorial English A–D ＜Quarter Course＞(hereinafter “the Student Guide”).
https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html
【Course profile】
・Each class has a maximum of 4 students.
・Lessons are offered twice a week (Saturday intensives are offered once a week, 2 periods in a row).
・Schedules differ between campuses, and each section is held only on one campus. Once course registration is complete, it cannot be changed.
・The course uses Tutorial Canvas, which can be accessed through the “Classes” tab under “Learning Support” on MyWaseda. Please note that Tutorial Canvas may not function properly on PCs that do not meet the system requirements.
The course is designed for students who fit one or more of the following descriptions:
・TOEFL iBT（Speaking）score: above 5  *taken on/before Jan 20, 2026: above 25
・TOEIC S&W（Speaking）score: above 180
・Who are aiming to understand and speak English at a fast, native pace on any subject, recognizing implicit meaning and the nuances of the words
【Levels】
Students are placed in levels and grouped into classes based on the results of the LANGX Test, which is taken during a specified period. The 4 levels are Basic, Intermediate, Upper Intermediate, and Advanced. The first three (Basic, Intermediate, and Upper Intermediate) are completed in four quarters A, B, C and D, which should be taken consecutively.
・Advanced is completed in two quarters, A and B, which should be taken consecutively.
It is recommended that students begin the course in spring semester or fall semester, taking A and B consecutively.
For students taking the course as an elective:
Students select the level of the course, which cannot be changed after registration. The LANGX test must be taken from the class registration screen at this time. Students can only register for A or C during the 1st registration period and need to take the test during the 1st registration period. Click “入力有” under “備考欄” to take the LANGX test.
For students who are required to take the course:
Student levels are determined by their LANGX Test scores. Compulsory students must take the LANGX Test during the designated testing period.
Please see https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html (LANGX test periods)
【Schedule】
Lessons offered twice a week
A lesson is offered on Monday, Tuesday or Wednesday for the first half of the week. The other lesson will be offered on Thursday, Friday or Saturday.

schedule_plan:
The course flow below is the same for both elective and compulsory students:
1.  Pre-Course LANGX test (approximately 30 minutes)
Please take the LANGX Test during the designated period. If you do not take the test, you may not be able to enroll in the appropriate level or class.
2.  Class announcements
Information about tutors, class days, times, and locations will be posted on Tutorial Canvas. Announcements will be made in the evening on the following dates:
Summer quarter: June 1 late afternoon
Winter quarter : November 16 late afternoon
3.  Class meetings
Each class has specific “Can-dos” (learning goals). To achieve the Can-dos, students will learn vocabulary and expressions and practice using them in conversations.
①
Preparation
Before each class, students must complete the Preparation activities on Tutorial Canvas (about 40–60 minutes). These activities help students think about the topic in advance and prepare to participate actively in class.
②
In class
All classes are held on campus. Students practice conversations through pair and group work, as well as role-play activities. Students are assessed on their interactions in class, which include turn-taking, active listening, and working with others. Assessment scores and feedback will be posted on Tutorial Canvas.
③
Test Unit
Units 5 and 10 are designated as Test Units:
Unit 5: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 1–4.
Unit 10: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 6–9.
The lesson flow in Test Units is similar to regular units, but students will be specifically evaluated on whether they can use the target Can-dos correctly and effectively.
④
Final Review Sheet
After the quarter, students will receive a Final Review Sheet from each tutor. It will include comments on the student’s progress and strengths, along with advice for future study.
⑤
LANGX (Post-Course)　(approx. 30 minutes)
After Unit 10, students are required to take the LANGX test again to assess their progress.
The following are the topics for each unit.
Unit 1 Culture (1)
Unit 2 Culture (2)
Unit 3 Social Issues (1)
Unit 4 Social Issues (2)
Unit 5 Test Unit (Unit 1-4)
Unit 6 Complex Issues (1)
Unit 7 Complex Issues (2)
Unit 8 Science and Technology (1)
Unit 9 Science and Technology (2)
Unit 10 Test Unit (Unit 6-9)

The course is designed for students who fit one or more of the following descriptions:
・TOEFL iBT（Speaking）score: above 5  *taken on/before Jan 20, 2026: above 25
・TOEIC S&W（Speaking）score: above 180
・Who are aiming to understand and speak English at a fast, native pace on any subject, recognizing implicit meaning and the nuances of the words
【Levels】
Students are placed in levels and grouped into classes based on the results of the LANGX Test, which is taken during a specified period. The 4 levels are Basic, Intermediate, Upper Intermediate, and Advanced. The first three (Basic, Intermediate, and Upper Intermediate) are completed in four quarters A, B, C and D, which should be taken consecutively.
・Advanced is completed in two quarters, A and B, which should be taken consecutively.
It is recommended that students begin the course in spring semester or fall semester, taking A and B consecutively.
For students taking the course as an elective:
Students select the level of the course, which cannot be changed after registration. The LANGX test must be taken from the class registration screen at this time. Students can only register for A or C during the 1st registration period and need to take the test during the 1st registration period. Click “入力有” under “備考欄” to take the LANGX test.

Student levels are determined by their LANGX Test scores. Compulsory students must take the LANGX Test during the designated testing period.
Please see https://led.w-as.jp/guide.html (LANGX test periods)

Preparation

In class

Unit 5: assessment covers Can-dos from Units 1–4.

After Unit 10, students are required to take the LANGX test again to assess their progress.

Unit 5 Test Unit (Unit 1-4)
Unit 6 Complex Issues (1)
Unit 7 Complex Issues (2)
Unit 8 Science and Technology (1)
Unit 9 Science and Technology (2)
